compiled_state.description:
## Context

Preserve the reconciler's uncommitted inbound events and bridge-bot authorship before the raw workflow commit-back is removed. The push-only primitive from [rebar:953a-d616-52d3-4efe] cannot stage or commit a dirty tracker, and existing callers depend on that push-only contract.

## Approach

- Add `commit_and_push_tickets_branch(tracker, *, message, strict=False, author_name=None, author_email=None)` in `src/rebar/_store/push.py`.
- Resolve the canonical tracker, then acquire its existing write lock.
- Before inspecting or staging a dirty tree, reuse `lock.check_no_rebase_in_progress`. A guarded rebase/merge-recovery state must never be committed: strict mode raises the dependency-defined `PushDeliveryError` with the existing `merge-recovery-blocked` reason; default best-effort mode logs a warning and returns without staging, committing, or pushing.
- When the recovery guard is clear, inspect the dirty tree under the lock, stage all tracker changes, and commit only when dirty.
- Apply supplied identity per commit with `git -c user.name=... -c user.email=...`; use ambient identity when omitted and never mutate global or repository config.
- Release the write lock before delegating to `push_tickets_branch`, avoiding nested push/merge locks.
- Delegate to `push_tickets_branch` unconditionally after a successful optional-commit phase, even when the tree is clean, because an already-committed local-ahead HEAD still needs delivery. Under strict mode a persistent rejection on this clean/ahead path raises the dependency-defined `PushDeliveryError`; it never returns success while commits remain local-only.
- Strict lock, staging, or commit failures raise the exact reusable `PushDeliveryError` defined by [rebar:953a-d616-52d3-4efe], using stable `commit-lock-timeout`, `stage-failed`, and `commit-failed` reasons. Core never exits the process or writes process streams.
- Default `strict=False` preserves the store's best-effort disposition for lock, stage, and commit failures: log a warning, return without calling the push primitive, retain the uncommitted content for recovery, and allow a later clean retry to commit and deliver it. A failed commit may leave the index staged, but must not lose content or create/push a commit; the retry must succeed.
- Keep direct `push_tickets_branch` completely push-only.
- Extend the dependency-provided private adapter at `python -m rebar._store.push` with `commit-and-push --tracker ... --message ... [--strict] [--author-name ... --author-email ...]`; retain its existing `push --tracker ... [--strict]` action unchanged. Both actions share the one dependency-defined `PushDeliveryError` translation boundary; `--strict` maps to the core `strict=True` keyword and no second exception or stderr path is introduced.

## Testing

Use real temporary repositories for dirty, clean/ahead, supplied-identity, ambient-identity, recovery-guard, and retry contracts. Add the composed operation to the existing two-clone shared concurrency suite because this task combines a locked commit with a later push/reconciliation.

RED-first oracle:
- a dirty tracker and bare origin remain uncommitted/unpublished under the current push-only API;
- held out: supplied identity appears in `git show`; omitted identity uses the ambient repository identity;
- held out: clean/ahead state pushes without an empty commit; a paired persistent-rejection case preserves the local commit and raises `PushDeliveryError` in core, with the module CLI returning nonzero;
- held out: a real rebase/merge-recovery marker blocks the commit path before staging; strict raises `merge-recovery-blocked`, default mode warns/returns, content remains recoverable, and a clean retry after recovery succeeds;
- held out: injected lock, stage, and commit failures distinguish strict typed errors from default warn-and-return behavior, prove no push occurs, retain the dirty content/local commit, and succeed on a clean retry;
- held out: direct `push_tickets_branch` neither stages nor commits a dirty tracker;
- held out: real module-CLI subprocesses prove the new `commit-and-push` action routes all flags, and the dependency-provided `push` action plus its sole exception translation remain green;
- held out: competing remote and local events both survive through the two-clone barrier;
- mutation bypassing the commit makes the dirty-tree oracle RED; removing the recovery guard makes the pending-picks oracle RED; removing per-command identity makes the authorship oracle RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A dirty tracker is committed and delivered to origin through `commit_and_push_tickets_branch`.
- [x] A clean but locally-ahead tracker is pushed without creating an empty commit; when persistent rejection prevents convergence under strict mode, the local commit stays reachable and core raises the dependency-defined `PushDeliveryError` (the module CLI returns nonzero) rather than reporting success.
- [x] Supplied name/email and ambient fallback identities are both proven from commit author metadata.
- [x] The entrypoint never mutates global or repository git identity configuration.
- [x] Concurrent remote and local events both remain reachable through the shared two-clone contention harness.
- [x] Direct `push_tickets_branch` remains push-only and preserves a dirty worktree.
- [x] Real `python -m rebar._store.push` subprocess tests prove the new `commit-and-push` action routes tracker/message/strict/identity arguments, while the dependency-provided `push` action remains unchanged.
- [x] A real rebase/merge-recovery state is rejected before staging or committing: strict mode raises the dependency-defined `PushDeliveryError` with `merge-recovery-blocked`; default mode warns and returns without push; after recovery, a clean retry commits and delivers the retained content.
- [x] Strict lock, staging, and commit failures raise the exact dependency-defined catchable `PushDeliveryError` with the named reasons; core never calls `sys.exit`, and the shared private CLI boundary alone translates it to the same stderr/nonzero contract.
- [x] Default-mode lock, staging, and commit failures warn and return without invoking push or losing dirty content; a later clean retry commits and delivers that content.
- [x] [operator-attested] Focused pytest nodes, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass.

## Compatibility and rollback

The entrypoint is internal and initially unused, so it can land independently without affecting old workflows or vocabulary. Existing `push_tickets_branch` callers retain their push-only, best-effort behavior. Revert the later workflow-cutover change before reverting this prerequisite.
